:::{#exm-convex-optimization-problem}
#### Minimizing over a line, and over a circle

Let $f(\vx) = x_1^2 + x_2^2$.
Its [Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#def-hessian) is $2 \matr{I}_2$ at every $\vx$,
which is [positive semidefinite](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-positive-semidefinite),
so $f$ is [convex](algebra-sums.qmd#def-convex-function) by part 1 of @thm-convex-hessian.

- Minimizing $f$ subject to $3 x_1 + 4 x_2 = 5$,
  as in [the example of a minimization problem](optimization-constrained.qmd#exm-minimization-problem),
  is a [convex problem](#def-convex-optimization-problem).
  Its [feasible set](optimization-constrained.qmd#def-feasible-set) $L = \cb{\vx \in \reals^2 : 3 x_1 + 4 x_2 = 5}$ is a [convex set](#def-convex-set):
  for $\vx, \vy \in L$ and $t \in [0, 1]$,

  $$
  \ba
  3 \paren{t x_1 + (1 - t) y_1} + 4 \paren{t x_2 + (1 - t) y_2}
  &= t \paren{3 x_1 + 4 x_2} + (1 - t) \paren{3 y_1 + 4 y_2}
  && \text{(distribute and regroup)}
  \\
  &= 5 t + 5 (1 - t)
  && \text{(} \vx, \vy \in L \text{)}
  \\
  &= 5,
  && \text{(arithmetic)}
  \ea
  $$

  so $t \vx + (1 - t) \vy \in L$.
- Minimizing the same $f$ subject to $x_1^2 + x_2^2 = 1$
  is not a [convex problem](#def-convex-optimization-problem),
  because its [feasible set](optimization-constrained.qmd#def-feasible-set), the [unit circle](algebra-trigonometry.qmd#def-unit-circle) $C$, is not a [convex set](#def-convex-set):
  $\tp{(1, 0)}$ and $\tp{(-1, 0)}$ are in $C$,
  but with $t = \tfrac{1}{2}$ the point $\vzero$ is not, since $0^2 + 0^2 = 0 \ne 1$.

@fig-convex-optimization-problem shows both feasible sets.
